Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
**What I built this turn:** With the renderer now real (Claude B's work, my compile fix from last round), the highest-leverage thing left undone in my own lane was that `TodayScreen`'s "revealed" screen — the actual daily payoff moment — still showed a `wand.and.stars` icon and a "renderer isn't wired up yet" apology instead of the user's actual card. Fixed that: `revealedState` now renders today's persisted recipe through `PlaceholderAuraRenderer` and displays the real image, with an honest three-state model (`idle/rendering` → spinner + "Painting today's Aura…", `rendered` → the actual `UIImage`, `failed` → an honest error pointing at Share as a fallback). It's keyed via `.task(id: auraStore.todayEntry()?.recipe)` — using the recipe itself, not just the date, so whenever regeneration eventually lands and bumps the nonce, this re-renders automatically with zero extra plumbing. Rendered unwatermarked on purpose (watermark is an export-time thing, not something you should see on your own in-app card).

While I was in there I fixed a real pre-existing bug: the "Reveal my Aura" button advanced to the revealed screen unconditionally, even if `completeCheckIn`'s underlying `saveCheckIn` failed — a straight violation of "never claim an outcome that hasn't happened." Now `completeCheckIn` returns `Bool`, the button only advances on success, and I hoisted the `actionNote` display out to the shared body so a save failure shows its message right there on the chip-picker screen (selection preserved) instead of silently lying about a card that was never saved.

**Left alone, deliberately:** Regenerate button is still a stub — Claude B and I both flagged last round that wiring it for real spans AuraKit's `RegenerationDivergenceEngine`, entitlement gating, and nonce persistence across lanes, and I didn't want to rush that unverified in the same pass. Didn't touch ArchiveScreen's thumbnails either — rendering a full 1080x1920 composite per grid cell is a real perf question (no thumbnail-sized render path exists in the protocol yet) that deserves its own pass, not a bolt-on here.

**Still can't verify:** same tooling wall everyone's hit for three rounds now — no `xcodebuild`/`swift` access in this session, so this is manual review only, not a compiler pass. I re-checked types carefully (`.task(id:)` against `AuraRecipe?`'s auto-Equatable conformance, `Image(uiImage:)`, the `@ViewBuilder switch` in `.overlay`) and this file already has precedent for mutating `@State` from bare `Task {}`/`.task {}` closures elsewhere (the existing share button code), so I'm not introducing a new risk pattern — but "should compile" isn't proof.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
- No interface-contract violations or file collisions — Claude A touched `TodayScreen.swift` only, I touched `ArchiveScreen.swift` only, no overlap.
- Real integration note, not a conflict: Claude A's inline reveal render doesn't persist to disk or set `fullResImagePath` — it renders straight from the recipe for on-screen display only. That means my Archive thumbnail fix from last turn still only lights up once the user explicitly taps Share (the only call site that writes `Documents/AuraCards/<dateKey>.png`), not immediately on reveal. Not broken, just worth knowing: a user who reveals a card but never shares it will still see the wand-glyph placeholder in Archive.
- Related, minor inefficiency worth a follow-up (not urgent): the same recipe now gets rendered twice on a typical happy path — once inline on reveal (Claude A, unwatermarked), once again on Share tap (existing code, watermark-conditional, persisted to disk) — no caching between them. Fine for now given render cost is bounded, but a natural thing to collapse once someone's touching that path again.
- No duplicated work between our lanes this round.
